category: fully managed Redis and Redis Stack, free 30 MB Essentials plan on shared infrastructure

free_tier.stated: Free plan: Always $0, up to 30 MB, a 30 MB single database on a shared cloud deployment, best-effort SLA and community support. The 30 MB Essentials plan is free and is designed for learning and building test projects.
free_tier.notes: Free plans are a type of Essentials plan, which gives an upgrade path to paid Essentials. Since Jan 2024 a new Essentials subscription supports only one database.

per_object_cap.stated: 30 MB database size on the free plan; the database size includes replication where applicable
per_object_cap.notes: bytes is the decimal reading of 30 MB as the vendor states it; the size includes replication where applicable, so the usable dataset is smaller when replication is on.

retention.stated: no expiry or inactivity deletion clock is stated on the pages read; the free database persists while the account and subscription are kept
retention.notes: null is indefinite: the pages read state no automatic expiry for the free database.

egress.terms: Data transfer is included in the price but limited on the Free plan; the free 30 MB Essentials plan has a 5 GB monthly total network bandwidth limit applied to the whole plan.
egress.free_allowance: 5 GB monthly total network bandwidth on the 30 MB free plan

interface_detail: the Redis protocol over TLS for clients; a REST API for subscription and database management
tooling: redis-cli, Redis Insight, and Redis client libraries for .NET, node.js, Python, Java, Go and PHP
chaining: a free Redis Cloud database can be added to a project through the Vercel Redis Cloud integration or the Heroku add-on, or reached directly from an application; the 30 MB and 100 ops/sec caps are the ceiling

limits.value: 30 MB database size, single database per Essentials subscription since Jan 2024
Maximum throughput 100 ops/sec on the 30 MB free plan; 30 concurrent connections
5 GB monthly total network bandwidth on the free plan; 1 CIDR allow rule

binding_note: the 30 MB single database is the hard ceiling that stops any workload first; the 100 ops/sec throughput and 5 GB transfer are generous relative to that 30 MB

identity_cost.detail: Signup offers two options: enter your information in the form and select Get Started, or sign up with Google or Github. After entering your information you receive an activation email from Redis and select Activate account. No card is requested for the free database; a card is added only when a paid tier is chosen.

reliability_note: best-effort SLA and community support on the free plan; Redis notifies the user before limiting database usage when the bandwidth or throughput limits are exceeded
confidence_note: four first-party Redis pages were captured and quoted on 2026-11-19: the pricing page, the Essentials plan details table, the quick start, and the RedisLabs support knowledge-base article. No probe was run; every figure is from a first-party page.

notes: The free Redis Cloud plan is 30 MB with one database, 30 connections, 100 ops/sec and 5 GB of transfer. It clears identity (no card) and interface (a real Redis protocol with clients), but the 30 MB ceiling is a hard wall, so the verdict is fails-quota. This is the RedisLabs hosted service, not the Redis Software that a user installs and runs; self-hosted Redis is not the offer here.
